summary: The exact candidate adds and validates useful hierarchical profiling for scheduler-worker and model-loading initialization, but it starts after spawned-worker module imports and omits parent-side launch work. An independent fresh-process import of gpu_worker took 11.383 seconds, and the retained Qwen timeline shows approximately ten seconds outside its 20.936-second tree. This is a partial original-issue fix, not a full launch-time breakdown.

gpu_evidence: The review node exposed one AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950, but Qwen-Image weights were absent from this review runtime. The candidate's retained Qwen log was inspected as candidate evidence, not represented as an independent review execution.
remaining_counterexamples: Spawned-worker Python/model dependency imports occur before run_scheduler_process and are absent from the timing tree; a fresh gpu_worker import took 11.383 seconds.
The candidate's retained Qwen run spans about 31 seconds from its first timestamp to profile emission while the root phase reports only 20.936 seconds, leaving roughly ten seconds unattributed.
Parent CLI/import preparation, multiprocessing pipe/process setup, process start overhead, and parent wait-for-ready duration are not measured or aggregated.
Calling log_startup_summary twice logs twice despite its log-once wording.
remaining_limitations: No Qwen-Image model weights were available in the review runtime, so the candidate's GPU launch was not independently rerun.
Only AMD MI355X gfx950 hardware was visible; multi-GPU, CUDA, XPU, MPS, NPU, and disaggregated paths were not exercised.
No native source changed, so native rebuild was not applicable.
Instrumentation does not change model numerics; no independent numerical reference was applicable to the reviewed code path.
